newsitem.title: USA: Lilly osteoporosis drug gets FDA priority.
newsitem.headline: Lilly osteoporosis drug gets FDA priority.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Wednesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted priority review status to Lilly's new drug application for raloxifene, an investigational compound for the prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis.

On the basis of the FDA's determination of the potential therapeutic significance of the drug, the agency has placed raloxifene on a six-month review schedule, in contrast to the standard 12-month review, Lilly said in a news release.
Lilly cautioned that this classification is not an assurance of a decision within six months, nor is it a guarantee of approval. The FDA may reclassify the application status at any time, it said.

Raloxifene is among the first in a new class of drugs called selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), which may provide an alternative to hormone replacement therapy in the prevention of postmenopausal health risks, including osteoporosis.
SERMs are being studied for their ability to act like estrogen in the skeleton and the cardiovascular system, without mimicking estrogen's effects in the breast and uterus.
